Definition: to yield up; intensively, to precipitate
BiblicalUsage: Magar means to cast down, to throw to the ground, and it appears twice. Ezekiel 21:12 has terrors by reason of the sword falling on the princes of Israel, and Psalms 89:44 says God made the king's glory to cease and cast his throne down to the ground.
TheologicalSignificance: I hold that Psalms 89:44 is the harder half: when God casts a throne down, even the anointed king feels the fall.
